ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The solutions in the two arms of this U-tube are separated by a membrane that is permeable to water and sodium chloride, but not to sucrose. Side A is filled with a solution of 0.6 M sucrose and 0.2 M sodium chloride (NaCl), and side B is filled with a solution of 0.2 M sucrose and 0.3 M NaCl. Initially, the volume on both sides is the same.

If you examine side A after a couple of days, you will see

method.method_draft: Track what can move over a couple of days. NaCl can cross the membrane, so its initial higher concentration on side B will not by itself keep water on side B; it tends to equilibrate between sides. Sucrose cannot cross, and because initial volumes are equal, side A contains more trapped sucrose than side B. To dilute the trapped sucrose on side A and balance the osmotic pressure, water flows into side A until the extra hydrostatic pressure of a taller column offsets the osmotic pull. Thus side A ends with a higher water level than initially.
